title: Pharmacophore-based identification and in Silico characterization of microbial metabolites as potential modulators of Wnt signaling pathway in colorectal cancer therapy.
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦微生物代谢物对Wnt通路中Tankyrase和β-catenin的抑制，属于蛋白-小分子药物筛选，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Aberrant activation of the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway, primarily driven by APC mutation and AXIN degradation via Tankyrase, contributes significantly to colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis. The accumulation of beta-catenin, resulting from the dysregulated ubiquitination, underscores the need for alternative therapeutic strategies targeting Tankyrase and beta-catenin. This present study explores microbial metabolites as a source of novel anti-cancer agents, leveraging their unique bioactivity and structural diversity, often exhibiting superior target specificity and lower toxicity than synthetic drugs. Through a computational drug discovery pipeline, a large library of 27641 microbial metabolites was initially screened based on multiple drug-likeliness criteria, resulting in the selection of 2527 compounds. Among the screened compounds, an integrated computational workflow comprising molecular docking, molecular dynamic simulations (MDS), MM/PBSA analysis, and Principal component analysis (PCA) identified Terreustoxin I (T1) as a potential Tankyrase inhibitor. In contrast, compound 10- phenyl-[12]-cytochalasin Z16 (B1) demonstrated a strong binding affinity within the beta-catenin active site. Under physiological conditions, these lead compounds were evaluated for conformational stability, binding efficacy, and dynamic behavior. Additionally, ADMET profiling, physiochemical properties, and bioactivity score predictions confirmed the identified compounds' pharmacokinetic suitability and reduced toxicity profile. In silico, cytotoxicity predictions showed significant activity against SW480 and HCT90 colorectal cell lines, with additional anti-neoplastic and anti-leukemic properties, strengthening their candidacy as effective anti-cancer agents. These findings provide a foundation for further experimental validation and development of novel CRC therapies with improved safety and efficacy potential.
abstract_zh: Wnt/β-catenin信号通路的异常激活，主要由APC突变和Tankyrase介导的AXIN降解驱动，对结直肠癌（CRC）的进展和转移有显著贡献。由泛素化失调导致的β-catenin积累，凸显了针对Tankyrase和β-catenin的替代治疗策略的必要性。本研究探索微生物代谢物作为新型抗癌药物的来源，利用其独特的生物活性和结构多样性，这些代谢物通常表现出优于合成药物的靶点特异性和较低毒性。通过计算药物发现流程，基于多种药物相似性标准，对包含27641种微生物代谢物的大型库进行了初步筛选，最终选出2527种化合物。在筛选出的化合物中，一个整合的计算工作流程，包括分子对接、分子动力学模拟（MDS）、MM/PBSA分析和主成分分析（PCA），将Terreustoxin I（T1）识别为潜在的Tankyrase抑制剂。相比之下，化合物10-苯基-[12]-细胞松弛素Z16（B1）在β-catenin活性位点内表现出强结合亲和力。在生理条件下，对这些先导化合物的构象稳定性、结合效力和动态行为进行了评估。此外，ADMET分析、理化性质和生物活性评分预测确认了所识别化合物的药代动力学适用性和降低的毒性特征。在计算机模拟中，细胞毒性预测显示对SW480和HCT90结直肠细胞系具有显著活性，并具有额外的抗肿瘤和抗白血病特性，增强了其作为有效抗癌药物的候选资格。这些发现为进一步的实验验证和开发具有改善安全性和有效性潜力的新型CRC疗法奠定了基础。
